title: U.S. House · Washington's 7th District
area: Most of the city of Seattle and nearby suburbs including Shoreline, Burien, and Vashon Island.

context.text: Washington uses a top-two primary open to all voters regardless of party. Incumbent Pramila Jayapal and Nirav Sheth advanced from the August 4, 2026 primary, defeating Gwen Kirkland (D) and David Blomstrom (Fifth Republic Party). Jayapal won the primary with 83.8% of the vote.

summary.text: Pramila Jayapal is the Democratic incumbent for Washington's 7th Congressional District. Born in India, she worked in global public health and founded the immigrant-advocacy organization OneAmerica before serving in the Washington State Senate (2015-2016) and winning election to Congress in 2016. According to her official biography, she is serving her fifth term and is a Chair Emerita of the Congressional Progressive Caucus.

background.text: Born in Chennai, India, in 1965. Her official biography says she grew up in India, Indonesia and Singapore and came to the United States by herself at age 16 to attend college.

Earned a bachelor's degree in English literature from Georgetown University in 1986 and a master's degree in marketing from Northwestern University in 1990 (her official biography describes the Northwestern degree as an MBA).

Worked as a financial analyst for PaineWebber Incorporated, and her official biography says she spent almost a decade in global health and development at the international nonprofit Program for Appropriate Technology in Health (PATH).

Founded OneAmerica, which her official biography describes as the largest immigrant advocacy organization in Washington State, and served as its executive director for 12 years; she also co-chaired the group We Belong Together.
Published two books: Pilgrimage to India: A Woman Revisits Her Homeland (2000) and Use the Power You Have: A Brown Woman's Guide to Politics and Political Change.
Served as a Democratic member of the Washington State Senate representing District 37 from 2015 to 2016, before her election to Congress.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2016 and now serving her fifth term; her official biography describes her as the first South Asian American woman elected to the House.

For the 2025-2026 Congress, serves on the House Judiciary Committee (Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement, and a member of the Subcommittee on the Constitution and Limited Government), the Foreign Affairs Committee (Subcommittees on Africa and on South and Central Asia), and the Budget Committee.

Her official site lists her as a Senior Whip of the Democratic Caucus and a Chair Emerita of the Congressional Progressive Caucus after six years as co-chair and sole chair; it names the Medicare for All bill, the College for All Act and the Ultra-Millionaire Tax Act among legislation she has authored or led.

positions.summary: Is a lead sponsor of the Medicare for All Act and says Medicare for All is the path to fix the health care system.
positions.quote: Medicare for All is the path to fix the broken healthcare system that has let corporate interests determine who lives and dies.

positions.summary: Led a War Powers Resolution to end U.S. hostilities in Iran, saying Congress was not consulted and that the war is unconstitutional.
positions.quote: From the beginning, this war has had no clear mission, no strategy, no end goal. Congress has not been consulted.

positions.summary: As Ranking Member of the House Judiciary immigration subcommittee, criticized the administration's mass deportation agenda and ICE arrest and detention practices.
positions.quote: ICE’s own data shows that the majority of people they arrest have ZERO criminal charges or convictions.

summary.text: Nirav Sheth is the Republican nominee for Washington's 7th Congressional District. According to his campaign website, he was born and raised in India, came to the United States in 2008 as a student, served in the Marine Corps, became a police officer in Lakewood, Washington, and now owns small businesses in Pierce County. He also ran in the 2024 Republican primary in Washington's 10th District and says he is running on public safety, infrastructure, small-business support and local control of education.

background.text: According to his campaign website, was born and raised in India and came to the United States in 2008 as a student of computer and electrical engineering; he says English is his fourth language.
Earned an associate degree from the Government Polytechnic State Institute of Gujarat in India in 2006.
Served in the U.S. Marine Corps from 2011 to 2014; his campaign website says he served as an aircraft mechanic and military police officer.
Describes himself on Ballotpedia as having been a homeless college student and as having assisted the liaison for U.S. Border Patrol intelligence.
Career experience listed on Ballotpedia includes working as an electrical engineer, in computer science, as an aircraft mechanic, as an automotive service advisor, and in property management.
According to his campaign website, became a police officer in Lakewood, Washington, in 2017.
Describes himself as a legal immigrant who worked his way from being homeless into becoming a small business owner in Pierce County; Ballotpedia says he owns several small businesses.
Ran as a Republican in the 2024 top-two primary for Washington's 10th Congressional District, receiving 11.7% of the vote and not advancing to the general election.
Advanced from the August 4, 2026 top-two primary in the 7th District, finishing second with 10.6% of the vote behind Jayapal.

priorities.text: Lists public safety, education, strong infrastructure, and immigration as his campaign's core issues.

positions.summary: Supports using state funding from HB 2015 to hire more police officers, with money going to recruitment, training and retention.
positions.quote: Support funding from HB 2015 to hire more police

positions.summary: Campaign education page calls for passing the Protecting Fairness in Girls' Sports initiative and cites federal guidance defining sex under Title IX.
positions.quote: Pass the Protecting Fairness in Girls’ Sports initiative to preserve opportunity and safety for female athletes.

positions.summary: Campaign affordability page criticizes the proposed Washington "millionaires tax" as part of what he calls a layering of state taxes.
positions.quote: Adding the “millionaires tax” with the claim of fixing our “regressive” tax code while refusing to lower the most regressive tax — our sales tax.

Jayapal's official house.gov and campaign websites did not yield fetchable issue-position text (menus and JavaScript-rendered content only), so her priorities and positions sections are left empty rather than inferred; her biography and committee assignments are sourced from her official house.gov pages and Ballotpedia. Jayapal's federal key votes and FEC totals are added separately by script. Sheth's biography relies on his campaign website and Ballotpedia; no independent news profile was found.
